solution_overview:
A survey asks respondents about their usage of three social media platforms: P, Q, and R. We are given the probabilities of using each platform individually, in pairs, and all three. We use the Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion and Venn diagram logic to compute probabilities of various event combinations.

Let $P, Q, R$ be the events that a randomly selected respondent uses Platform P, Q, or R, respectively. The given probabilities are:

$$P(P) = 0.60$$ 
$$P(Q) = 0.48$$ 
$$P(R) = 0.36$$ 
$$P(P \cap Q) = 0.28$$ 
$$P(P \cap R) = 0.20$$ 
$$P(Q \cap R) = 0.18$$ 
$$P(P \cap Q \cap R) = 0.12$$

To calculate the probability of using exactly one platform, exactly two platforms, or at least one platform, it is helpful to visualize the disjoint regions of a Venn diagram. Let $N_1$ be the probability of using exactly one platform, $N_2$ the probability of using exactly two platforms, and $N_3$ the probability of using exactly three platforms.

We are given $P(P \cap Q \cap R) = 0.12$, which is $N_3$.

The probability of using exactly two platforms, $N_2$, is the sum of the probabilities of using only P and Q, only P and R, and only Q and R. Each pairwise intersection includes the triple intersection, so we subtract $P(P \cap Q \cap R)$ from each pairwise intersection to get the 'only two' part.

$$N_2 = P(P \cap Q \cap R^c) + P(P \cap R \cap Q^c) + P(Q \cap R \cap P^c)$$

This simplifies to the sum of pairwise intersections minus three times the triple intersection:

$$N_2 = P(P \cap Q) + P(P \cap R) + P(Q \cap R) - 3 P(P \cap Q \cap R)$$

$$N_2 = 0.28 + 0.20 + 0.18 - 3(0.12)$$
$$N_2 = 0.66 - 0.36$$
$$N_2 = 0.30$$

The probability of using exactly one platform, $N_1$, is the sum of the individual platform probabilities minus twice the sum of pairwise intersections, plus three times the triple intersection. This accounts for elements counted multiple times in the sum of individual probabilities.

$$N_1 = P(P) + P(Q) + P(R) - 2(P(P \cap Q) + P(P \cap R) + P(Q \cap R)) + 3 P(P \cap Q \cap R)$$

$$N_1 = (0.60 + 0.48 + 0.36) - 2(0.28 + 0.20 + 0.18) + 3(0.12)$$
$$N_1 = 1.44 - 2(0.66) + 0.36$$
$$N_1 = 1.44 - 1.32 + 0.36$$
$$N_1 = 0.12 + 0.36$$
$$N_1 = 0.48$$
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

The probability that a respondent uses at least one platform, $P(P \cup Q \cup R)$, can be found using the Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion:

$$P(P \cup Q \cup R) = P(P) + P(Q) + P(R) - (P(P \cap Q) + P(P \cap R) + P(Q \cap R)) + P(P \cap Q \cap R)$$

Using the given values:

$$P(P \cup Q \cup R) = 0.60 + 0.48 + 0.36 - (0.28 + 0.20 + 0.18) + 0.12$$
$$P(P \cup Q \cup R) = 1.44 - 0.66 + 0.12$$
$$P(P \cup Q \cup R) = 0.78 + 0.12$$
$$P(P \cup Q \cup R) = 0.90$$

Since $0.90 = 90\%$, which exceeds $88\%$, the statement is True.

**B.** → False

The probability that the respondent uses exactly one platform is $N_1$. From the setup in the solution overview:

$$N_1 = 0.48$$

This means the probability is $48\%$. The claim states this probability is above $50\%$. Since $48\% \not> 50\%$, the statement is False.

**C.** → True

The probability that the respondent uses exactly two platforms is $N_2$. From the setup in the solution overview:

$$N_2 = 0.30$$

This means the probability is $30\%$. The claim states this probability is at least $28\%$. Since $30\% \ge 28\%$, the statement is True.

**D.** → True

The probability that a respondent uses none of the three platforms is the complement of using at least one platform, $P((P \cup Q \cup R)^c)$. We calculated $P(P \cup Q \cup R)$ in part A.

$$P(\text{none}) = 1 - P(P \cup Q \cup R)$$
$$P(\text{none}) = 1 - 0.90$$
$$P(\text{none}) = 0.10$$

This means the probability is $10\%$. The claim states this probability is under $12\%$. Since $10\% < 12\%$, the statement is True.

**E.** → True

The probability that a respondent uses at least two platforms includes those who use exactly two platforms and those who use exactly three platforms. This is the sum of $N_2$ and $N_3$.

$$P(\text{at least two}) = N_2 + N_3$$

From the solution overview, $N_2 = 0.30$ and $N_3 = P(P \cap Q \cap R) = 0.12$.

$$P(\text{at least two}) = 0.30 + 0.12$$
$$P(\text{at least two}) = 0.42$$

This means the probability is $42\%$. The claim states this probability exceeds $40\%$. Since $42\% > 40\%$, the statement is True.
